news.body: Analysts have held their fair value estimate for Indian Bank steady at about ₹1,001, citing only small tweaks in assumptions around the discount rate, revenue growth and future P/E as the reason for keeping the overall price target unchanged. What's in the News Board meeting scheduled for April 29, 2026, to consider and approve audited standalone and consolidated financial results for Q4 and the full year ended March 31, 2026.

news.title: Upcoming dividend of ₹18.25 per share
news.body: Eligible shareholders must have bought the stock before 10 June 2026. Payment date: 09 July 2026. Payout ratio is a comfortable 21% but the company is not cash flow positive. Trailing yield: 2.2%. Within top quartile of Indian dividend payers (1.5%). Higher than average of industry peers (1.5%).

news.title: INDIANB: Upcoming Dividend And Capital Plan Will Support Bullish Medium Term Outlook
news.body: Analysts have slightly increased their fair value estimate for Indian Bank from ₹998.08 to ₹1,001.54, reflecting somewhat higher assumed discount rates, modest adjustments to revenue growth and profit margin forecasts, and a revised future P/E of 13.94 in their updated pricing models. What's in the News Indian Bank announced an annual dividend of ₹18.25 per share, payable on July 17, 2026, with an ex date and record date of June 10, 2026 (Key Developments).

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹86.89 (vs ₹83.61 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹86.89 (up from ₹83.61 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹342.8b (up 11% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹117.0b (up 3.9% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 34% (down from 36% in FY 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Revenue is forecast to grow 13% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 1.6% growth forecast for the Banks industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 20% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 37% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.
